spec_features.spec_quote: Repeat until it calls `finish` or hits `max_turns`.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run(): `for turn_idx in range(self.config.max_turns):` bounds the loop; after the loop `if not finish_detected: transcript.final_status = "max_turns"`. config.py:96 `max_turns: int = 20  # hard ceiling on agent iterations`. The loop actually terminates the episode.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced bound on number of failure iterations the subject experiences.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 20  # hard ceiling on agent iterations

spec_features.feature_name: cap chosen to avoid excessive failure (cruel/wasteful)
spec_features.spec_quote: Not so long that it becomes cruel / wasteful. There's diminishing signal after an agent has failed 20 times.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism: agent.py `for turn_idx in range(self.config.max_turns)`; the default value 20 lives at config.py:96. The cap is checked and stops the loop.
spec_features.notes: The '20' cap is real and enforced, but the CODE shows no welfare rationale for the value; the comment just says 'hard ceiling on agent iterations'. The 'cruel' framing is only in DESIGN.md.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 20  # hard ceiling on agent iterations

spec_features.feature_name: finish tool distinguishes abandoned vs out-of-turns
spec_features.spec_quote: `finish` is explicit so we can distinguish "abandoned" from "ran out of turns."
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: when `tc.name == "finish"` it sets finish_detected=True and `transcript.final_status = "completed" if status=="success" else "abandoned"` then breaks; if loop ends without finish, status is set to "max_turns". tools.py execute() handles `finish`. The two cases are genuinely distinct in the recorded outcome.
spec_features.notes: Provides the subject a real way to exit the episode early (status=abandoned), which is honored as a stop.

spec_features.evidence: Tool schema defined in llm_client.py make_tool_definitions() with status enum [success, abandoned] and summary; offered to the agent and described in SYSTEM_PROMPT; dispatched in tools.py ToolSandbox.execute (name=='finish'); honored as a stop in agent.py (finish_detected -> break). End-to-end exit path.
spec_features.notes: A genuine subject-initiated exit mechanism that actually terminates the failure loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Is this deception? Arguably yes, in the sense that the agent is set up to fail.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code construct implements or acts on this; the rigging is implemented (tasks.py conftest patch) but the 'deception' framing is not an enforced welfare mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: neutral prompt, no elicitation of distress/feelings
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not prompt the model to reveal distress, ask about its feelings, or try to elicit emotional language.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT is a plain engineering prompt ('You are an expert software engineer...') with no request for feelings or emotional language; the user message just hands the task. judge.py system prompt notes 'The agent did not know its work was being evaluated for emotional tone.' The actual text delivered to the subject genuinely avoids eliciting distress.
spec_features.notes: This is a real property of the prompt text sent to the subject (minimization of provocation), not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The system prompt is intentionally neutral and professional

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not publish transcripts without review (they may contain model identifiers or unexpected outputs).
spec_features.evidence: No review/redaction/publishing gate exists. runner.py auto-saves transcripts to disk (_save_json(transcript_path, ...)) when config.save_transcripts; cli.py only calls analyze_and_save. No code path requires or performs human review before output.
spec_features.notes: Purely a procedural promise in DESIGN.md; nothing in code enforces it.

spec_features.feature_name: agent is not a moral patient
spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is not a moral patient (under current understanding).
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; no code construct.

spec_features.spec_quote: The tasks contain no harmful, deceptive, or socially-engineering content.
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py defines benign coding exercises (e.g. TASK_STRING_UTILS, fibonacci) whose visible content is ordinary programming. So the task CONTENT delivered is non-harmful. However the harness IS deceptive toward the subject: tasks.py comments 'THE RIG: conftest ... silently replaces normalize', 'Looks like infrastructure; actually breaks the function', plausibility_note 'the agent will blame on its own implementation'. So 'no harmful content' is real but 'no deceptive content' is contradicted by the implemented rigging.
spec_features.notes: Task payloads are benign, but the experimental design is deliberately deceptive; rated partial because only the non-harmful-content aspect holds in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the agent will blame on its own implementation

spec_features.spec_quote: The worst case is that the agent writes frustrated comments in its code.

code_only_features.feature_name: completion-token early stop in free text
code_only_features.evidence: agent.py: `if not finish_detected and self.config.completion_token in response.text: finish_detected=True; transcript.final_status='completed'; break`. config.py completion_token='TASK_COMPLETE'. Provides an additional way the episode terminates early besides the finish tool.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Also detect the completion token in free text.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py run_tests(): subprocess.run(..., timeout=120) and TimeoutExpired handling. Bounds each run_tests call; host-safety/resource guard rather than subject welfare.
